tasks.title: abort in flight
tasks.statement:
Spawn a task that prints "start", sleeps 100 ms and prints "end". After 20 ms cancel it (abort), await the handle and print "cancelled: true" (JoinError::is_cancelled).

Expected output:
`start`
`cancelled: true`
tasks.hint: let e = h.await.unwrap_err(); e.is_cancelled()

tasks.title: Drop of a cancelled future
tasks.statement:
Declare a struct Guard with a Drop that prints "drop guard". In select! the first branch is an async block that creates a Guard and sleeps 200 ms; the second sleeps 20 ms and prints "time-out". See what is printed and in what order: the losing future is destroyed together with its local values.

Expected output:
`drop guard`
`time-out`
tasks.hint: The Guard lives inside the async block and is destroyed when the block is dropped.

tasks.title: abort and is_finished
tasks.statement:
Spawn a task that sleeps 1 s, cancel it (abort), wait 10 ms and print "finished: true" based on is_finished().

Expected output:
`finished: true`
tasks.hint: After abort the task finishes at the nearest .await; is_finished() will show true.

tasks.title: A dropped handle does not cancel
tasks.statement:
Spawn a task: sleep 30 ms and print "running". Immediately drop the JoinHandle and wait 100 ms in main. The task must manage to print its line.

Expected output:
`running`
tasks.hint: drop(handle) does not call abort: the task stays alive.

tasks.title: A loop with a token
tasks.statement:
A task in a select! loop waits for tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken::cancelled() or a 10 ms sleep (count them). After 50 ms main cancels the token. The task prints "stopped", and main waits for it.

Expected output:
`stopped`
tasks.hint: tokio::select! { _ = token.cancelled() => break, _ = sleep(..) => n += 1 }

tasks.title: A tree of tokens
tasks.statement:
Create a parent token and a child one (child_token()). Cancel the parent and print "child: true" (child.is_cancelled()). Then create a new pair, cancel the child and print "parent: false".

Expected output:
`child: true`
`parent: false`
tasks.hint: Cancellation goes down the tree, but not up.

tasks.title: Waiting for the signal
tasks.statement:
The spawned task waits on token.cancelled().await and prints "signal received". Main (after a 20 ms pause) prints "cancelling", cancels the token and waits for the task.

Expected output:
`cancelling`
`signal received`
tasks.hint: cancel() wakes everyone waiting on cancelled().

tasks.title: The token's DropGuard
tasks.statement:
Get drop_guard() from a clone of the token in a separate block; after leaving the block print "cancelled: true" (token.is_cancelled()).

Expected output:
`cancelled: true`
tasks.hint: { let _g = token.clone().drop_guard(); }

tasks.title: Shutdown by broadcast
tasks.statement:
Spawn three worker tasks, each waiting for a stop message from a broadcast channel and returning its own number. After 20 ms main sends the signal, collects the numbers (JoinSet) and prints "stopped: 3".

Expected output:
`stopped: 3`
tasks.hint: let mut rx = tx.subscribe(); rx.recv().await; JoinSet::join_next().

tasks.title: TaskTracker
tasks.statement:
Spawn three tasks through a TaskTracker with sleeps of 10, 20 and 30 ms, close the tracker (close) and wait (wait). Print "all finished".

Expected output:
`all finished`
tasks.hint: use tokio_util::task::TaskTracker; tracker.spawn(..); tracker.close(); tracker.wait().await

tasks.title: JoinSet: sum
tasks.statement:
Spawn three tasks in a JoinSet that return 1, 2 and 3. Add up the results as they become ready (join_next) and print "sum: 6".

Expected output:
`sum: 6`
tasks.hint: while let Some(r) = set.join_next().await { sum += r.unwrap(); }

tasks.title: Cleanup on abort
tasks.statement:
A task creates a Guard with a Drop that prints "cleanup" and sleeps for a second. After 20 ms cancel it, await the handle and print "cancelled". The cleanup must happen first.

Expected output:
`cleanup`
`cancelled`
tasks.hint: Drop runs when the future is dropped, before h.await returns.

tasks.title: The concurrency limit
tasks.statement:
Process 10 jobs, limiting concurrency with a semaphore of 3 permits. In each job increment a counter of active jobs (AtomicUsize), update the maximum, sleep 30 ms and decrement. Print "peak: 3".

Expected output:
`peak: 3`
tasks.hint: fetch_max for the peak; keep the permit in a variable for the duration of the sleep.

tasks.title: Load shedding
tasks.statement:
A queue with 2 slots and no consumer. Send 5 jobs through try_send; count the accepted and the dropped (Full). Print "accepted 2, dropped 3".

Expected output:
`accepted 2, dropped 3`
tasks.hint: Err(TrySendError::Full(_)) => rejected += 1

tasks.title: Your own timeout error
tasks.statement:
Declare an enum Error { Timeout } (derive Debug) and async fn call() -> Result<u32, Error>: wait for a 200 ms sleep under a 30 ms timeout, and on expiry return Error::Timeout. Print the result of the call with {:?}.

Expected output:
«Err(Timeout)»
tasks.hint: .await.map_err(|_| Error::Timeout)?; then Ok(..)

tasks.title: spawn_blocking does not interfere
tasks.statement:
On a single-threaded runtime (flavor = "current_thread") spawn a ticker task: every 10 ms it increments a counter. Meanwhile await a spawn_blocking with a blocking std::thread::sleep of 100 ms. Then stop the ticker and print "ran in parallel: true" if there were at least 5 ticks.

Expected output:
`ran in parallel: true`
tasks.hint: spawn_blocking(|| std::thread::sleep(..)).await: while we wait, the runtime thread is free for the ticker.

tasks.title: Fix: a blocking sleep in a task
tasks.statement:
The ticker on a single-threaded runtime gets no time: main does the "heavy work" (std::thread::sleep for 100 ms) right in the asynchronous function. Move it into spawn_blocking so the ticker manages to fire at least 5 times: the output must be "ticks at least 5: true".

Expected output:
`ticks at least 5: true`
tasks.hint: tokio::task::spawn_blocking(|| std::thread::sleep(..)).await.unwrap();

tasks.title: A panic in a task
tasks.statement:
Spawn a task that panics (panic!), await the handle and print "panic: true" based on JoinError::is_panic(). The program must not crash.

Expected output:
`panic: true`
tasks.hint: let e = h.await.unwrap_err(); e.is_panic()

tasks.title: A supervisor
tasks.statement:
On its first two runs the task panics, on the third it finishes normally; each run prints "launch N". Write a supervisor loop: while the handle returns an error, start the task again. After success print "done".

Expected output:
`launch 1`
`launch 2`
`launch 3`
`done`
tasks.hint: An AtomicUsize counts the runs; if tokio::spawn(..).await.is_ok() { break }

tasks.title: Retries with a limit
tasks.statement:
The operation always fails (Err("fail")). Retry it at most 3 times with a 10 ms pause between attempts. Print "attempts: 3" and "result: Err".

Expected output:
`attempts: 3`
`result: Err`
tasks.hint: An attempt counter, a pause after each failure, exit on the limit.

tasks.title: Rate limiting with an interval
tasks.statement:
Process 5 events, before each one waiting for tick() of a 20 ms interval (the first tick is immediate). Print "limited: true" if everything took at least 70 ms.

Expected output:
`limited: true`
tasks.hint: Ticks at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80 ms: the last event is at 80 ms.

tasks.title: A token bucket
tasks.statement:
A semaphore with no permits and a background task: every 20 ms it adds one permit (add_permits(1)). Main takes three permits in a row (acquire().await.forget()). Print "refill works: true" if this took at least 55 ms.

Expected output:
`refill works: true`
tasks.hint: sem.acquire().await.unwrap().forget(): the token is spent, not returned.

tasks.title: Burst and waiting
tasks.statement:
A bucket of 3 tokens, initially full, refilled one token every 50 ms. Take 3 tokens (it must take less than 20 ms) and print "burst: true", then take a fourth and print "fourth waited: true" (at least 40 ms).

Expected output:
`burst: true`
`fourth waited: true`
tasks.hint: Measure Instant before and after acquire; refill in a background task.

tasks.title: Runtime metrics
tasks.statement:
In a plain fn main build a multi-threaded runtime with 2 worker threads (Builder, enable_all) and print rt.metrics().num_workers().

Expected output:
«2»
tasks.hint: tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().worker_threads(2).enable_all().build()

tasks.title: yield_now: give up the thread
tasks.statement:
On a single-threaded runtime spawn a task that raises a shared AtomicBool. In main wait for the flag to go up with a loop of tokio::task::yield_now().await (no sleep) and print "flag raised".

Expected output:
`flag raised`
tasks.hint: while !flag.load(Ordering::SeqCst) { tokio::task::yield_now().await; } — without yield_now the task would never get the thread.

tasks.title: The actor does not answer
tasks.statement:
An actor receives a request with a oneshot::Sender and "hangs" (sleeps 500 ms, no reply). The client waits for the reply with a 50 ms timeout and on expiry prints "actor did not reply".

Expected output:
`actor did not reply`
tasks.hint: timeout(Duration::from_millis(50), reply_rx).await.is_err()

tasks.title: Drain the queue
tasks.statement:
The producer sends 5 jobs and closes the channel. The consumer handles each one (sleep 5 ms) until the channel is closed and then prints "processed: 5": the queue is not lost on close.

Expected output:
`processed: 5`
tasks.hint: while let Some(_) = rx.recv().await exits only after all the messages have been read.

tasks.title: Stop takes priority
tasks.statement:
The token is already cancelled and there are jobs in the queue. A select! loop with biased; checks cancelled() first, then recv(). Print "after stop: 0", the number of jobs processed.

Expected output:
`after stop: 0`
tasks.hint: tokio::select! { biased; _ = token.cancelled() => break, job = rx.recv() => .. }

tasks.title: A stop flag through watch
tasks.statement:
Three workers wait until a watch value becomes true (rx.wait_for(|v| *v).await). After 20 ms main sends true and waits for all of them (JoinSet). Print "stopped: 3".

Expected output:
`stopped: 3`
tasks.hint: let (tx, rx) = watch::channel(false); in the task let mut rx = rx.clone(); rx.wait_for(|v| *v).await

tasks.title: Explicit close instead of async Drop
tasks.statement:
A struct Conn { closed: bool } with a Drop: if closed == false, it prints "not closed!". Add async fn close(mut self): it sets closed = true and sleeps 10 ms (imitating a buffer flush). Call close and print "closed explicitly". There must be no warning from Drop.

Expected output:
`closed explicitly`
tasks.hint: In close(mut self) set the flag before self is destroyed at the end of the function.
